headline: Cell-state-conditioned sequence models score noncoding variants, paired with single-cell perturbation readouts
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Modeling
summary: New models predict cell-type-specific variant effects while single-cell edit-and-expression assays provide experimental readouts linking perturbations to expression.
synthesis: The dominant thread is sequence-to-activity modeling that attributes noncoding variation to regulatory state in defined cellular contexts. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-conditioned regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb DNA and adds an enhancer-gene link atlas. ChromBPNet models across 17 hematopoietic cell types score 302,830 noncoding variants, reporting lineage-structured accessibility effects complementary to GWAS. Experimental counterparts couple genetic edits to single-cell readouts: Superb-seq jointly captures Cas9 edits and transcriptomes, detecting on- and off-target edits linked to expression changes in K562, and Perturb-Tags spatial multi-omic screens in embryoid bodies reveal non-autonomous responses, modeled with a GNN. The remaining items (isoform, methylation, fibrosis, platelet and lncRNA resources) are adjacent cell-type-resolved molecular atlases rather than variant-effect models.
